item.text:
I'll analyze each chunk against the Chapter 5B economic wellbeing lenses.

**U0061** — Pre-candidate registration (Dec 2017) and discourse (March 2018) referencing "Cuarta Transformación," "gobierno honesto," anti-corruption/anti-impunity pledges, no vengeance. No concrete economic policy, fiscal/monetary rule, budget outcome, distributional fact, or shock-response measure. Material only as adjacent campaign-rhetoric context for 5B.1/5B.5/5B.7.
**Decision: EXCLUDE.** Adjacent campaign-rhetoric context only; no concrete named policy action, measured outcome, cost, or distributional result. Generic slogans about anti-corruption and reconciliation do not meet the evidence test for 5B.

**U0062** — 2018 electoral program platform: "austeridad republicana" (fiscal adjustment reorienting current spending to investment, no tax hikes except border-zone cuts, no debt issuance); gradual minimum-wage increase to 171 pesos by end of sexenio; universal pension for older adults at 1,500 pesos/month; boosting domestic gasoline supply/refineries to cut imports; rolling back Peña Nieto energy reform; energy and food self-sufficiency with guarantee prices for producers.
**Decision: INCLUDE.** Lenses:
- 5B.1 — specific agenda items (austeridad, wage floor, pension floor, refinery expansion, energy/food self-sufficiency)
- 5B.3 — fiscal rules: no tax increases, no debt issuance, current-spending cuts
- 5B.6 — proposed infrastructure (refineries, guarantee prices for producers)
- 5B.8 — distributional: minimum-wage scale-up, pensions, border-zone tax cuts
- 5B.9 — relevant insofar as energy reform reversal is a planned shock-response

**U0063** — Insecurity chapter (National Guard, addressing social causes), rejecting association with Caracas; explicit programmatic positioning for 2018–2024: pragmatic social democracy accepting free market, free trade, macroeconomic stability, budgetary discipline, peso float, Banco de México autonomy — combined with rejection of neoliberalism, privatizations, and "foreignization" of strategic sectors; prioritization of national production, domestic consumption, horizontal growth across the country.
**Decision: INCLUDE.** Lenses:
- 5B.3 — explicit acceptance of macroeconomic stability, budgetary discipline, peso flotation, central-bank autonomy
- 5B.4 — market/trade posture, rejection of privatization
- 5B.1 — production/consumption priorities, horizontal growth
- 5B.5 — anti-corruption pledge to "set example" from Los Pinos (necessary adjacent context only for 5B.5; lens 5B.5 not strongly served here)
- 5B.6 — security capacity (National Guard) is adjacent but not a 5B.6 economic-infrastructure item; do not count as 5B.6 material
- 5B.9 — rejection of Chavismo and rejection of Trump's tariffs posture — partial adjacent context

**U0064** — Positions: rejection of grand coalition government with PRI/PAN ministers; legal mechanisms for revocation of elected mandates and desafuero of officials prosecuted for corruption; free nationwide Internet; closing gender labor gaps; Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro student stipend program; cancellation of NAIM (Texcoco) and use of Santa Lucía (AISL) military base as alternative; July 1, 2018 election results: 53.19% López Obrador, 64.4% turnout; Trump congratulatory tweet.
**Decision: INCLUDE.** Lenses:
- 5B.1 — Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, universal Internet, AISL alternative
- 5B.4 — labor/gender gap closure, free Internet as enabling infrastructure
- 5B.5 — revocation/desafuero mechanisms as anti-corruption legal tools
- 5B.6 — AISL/NAIM infrastructure choice (concrete project cancellation vs. reuse of existing military facilities)
- 5B.7 — election outcome / institutional context only adjacent; do not count as 5B.7 material
- 5B.10 — partial adjacent; long-term infrastructure setup

**U0065** — July 1, 2018 victory speech at Zócalo: principles "no mentir, no robar, no traicionar"; "transición con armonía"; "prefer attention to the poorest"; August 8, 2018 TEPJF validation of the election.
**Decision: EXCLUDE.** General victory-rhetoric material. No concrete named policy action, budget figure, distributional result, or implementation finding beyond slogans. Adjacent context only.

**U0066** — Congressional results: MORENA + allies hold absolute majorities — 308/500 deputies, 69/128 senators; gubernatorial sweep (CDMX/Sheinbaum, Chiapas, Tabasco, Veracruz; ally PES/Morelos); PAN retains Guanajuato/Puebla, gains Yucatán; MC Jalisco; MORENA most-voted in 18 of 27 state legislatures. Cobertura informativa hasta 6/8/2018.
**Decision: INCLUDE.** Lenses:
- 5B.1 — legislative majorities establish the institutional preconditions for enacting the 2018–2024 program
- 5B.5 — political capacity to pursue anti-corruption agenda (sheinbaum/CDMX etc. governance context adjacent)
- 5B.10 — institutional inheritance/constraints the administration must operate within
Note: This is structural/institutional fact material rather than enacted economic policy; cite only as adjacent institutional context for lenses 5B.1/5B.5/5B.10. It does not meet the named-policy-action test for most lenses but does meet the "attribution fact that could merit a distinct evidence record" bar for legislative composition relevant to 5B.10 (institutional constraints).

**U0067** — CIDOB institutional footer, contact info, recent searches, copyright.
**Decision: EXCLUDE.** Source boilerplate; no material evidence.
